name: McGill University
summary: McGill University is an English-language public research university in Montreal, Quebec; it received its royal charter in 1821. This record covers the BA in Economics (Faculty of Arts) and the BSc in Computer Science (Faculty of Science).

internationalShare.notes: Quick facts excerpt: 27% of total enrolment is international (50% Quebec, 23% rest of Canada); other McGill pages say 'nearly 30%'. Reporting year not confirmed.

applicationPlatform.value: McGill online application (Applicant Portal); documents uploaded to the portal

applicationFee.value: CAD 140.16 (non-refundable); a second application for the same term and level at no extra cost
applicationFee.notes: From a search excerpt of McGill's Apply page; confirm the fee for the Fall 2027 cycle.

testing.notes: For U.S. high school applicants for Fall 2027, submitting SAT or ACT scores is optional; McGill says doing so gives additional information early in the review.

english.waiver: Not required if you have lived and attended high school/university for at least four consecutive years in a country where English is the acknowledged primary language, or completed certain curricula (e.g. IB, A-Level) with qualifying grades.

english.minOverall: 90 (120-point scale, tests up to 20 Jan 2026); 4.5 on the new 6-point scale (tests from 21 Jan 2026)
english.minSection: 21 in reading, listening, writing and speaking (120-point scale); 4.5 each in reading, listening, writing and 4.0 in speaking (6-point scale)
english.notes: Some programs (Education, TESL, Management) require 100; not applicable to the programs listed here.

internationalTuition.notes: International undergraduates admitted for 2026-27: BA CAD 56,000.10 tuition per year; BSc CAD 54,000.00 per year; plus society and other fees (about CAD 700-725) and optional health insurance. Figures from a search excerpt of McGill's Student Accounts tuition PDF; rates for the 2027 intake were not retrieved.

scholarships.name: McGill One-Year Entrance Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students entering McGill for the first time into a first full-time undergraduate degree; all applicants are automatically considered, regardless of citizenship; no separate application.

scholarships.name: McGill Major Entrance Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Awarded on academic achievement and outstanding leadership by selection committees; open to new first-year students regardless of citizenship; transfer, mature, exchange, visiting and part-time students are not eligible.
scholarships.coverage: CAD 12,000-48,000 in total (CAD 3,000-12,000 per year, renewable for up to four years)
scholarships.notes: McGill's deadlines page lists a separate Major Entrance Scholarship application/document deadline of January 21; the year was not confirmed so no date is recorded.

deadlines.label: Application deadline: applicants in overseas or U.S. high schools

programs.name: Economics (BA), Faculty of Arts
programs.summary: BA with an Economics Major Concentration (36 credits) or Honours. Mastery of high-school mathematics is expected for all economics courses, and Honours Economics requires two semesters of calculus (met by IB, A-level, AP or French Baccalaureate calculus).

requirements.minimum: IB Diploma with grades of 5 or better on each HL and SL subject is the minimum expected for most programs
requirements.typical: 33 to 36 subject points (out of 42) for Faculty of Arts

subjects.subject: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.notes: Faculty of Arts has no specific admission prerequisites, but McGill accepts HL Math AA for programs with a mathematics prerequisite; SL Math AI is not accepted for those programs. Economics courses assume high-school mathematics mastery.

requirements.notes: Advanced standing: at least 3 accepted HL subjects with final grade 5 or better can earn 30 credits for a BA.

requirements.minimum: Minimum of three A-Levels in three different subjects
requirements.notes: Faculty of Arts has no specific A-level subject prerequisites; A-level mathematics with differential and some integral calculus can meet the Honours Economics calculus prerequisite. No grade requirement found in retrieved text.

All India Senior School Certificate accepted. Applicants are considered on Class X results, Class 11 and mid-year Class 12 school transcripts, or the final Class XII certificate; predicted grades are not used. No minimum percentage was found in retrieved text.
Indian School Certificate accepted on the same basis as CBSE; no minimum percentage found in retrieved text.
AP exam results (completed or expected) must be declared on the application; AP calculus can meet the Honours Economics calculus prerequisite.

requirements.minimum: U.S. high school diploma from an academic university-entrance program accredited by a U.S. regional accreditation agency
requirements.typical: B+ average (unweighted) in each of grades 11 and 12 and B+ in each English course (Faculty of Arts)

fees.notes: International, admitted 2026-27; rate guaranteed for the program's duration without a break in enrolment.
